verses.1: On that day, when Jesus left the house, he sat down by the sea.
verses.2: Many people gathered around him, so that he could sit in the boat. Every person in the crowd stood on the deck of the boat.
verses.3: And he spoke to them in many parables, saying, “Look! The shepherd has come.”
verses.4: And in the process of feeding him, some of what fell along the way were eaten by birds as he went along.
verses.5: But other parts fell onto the rocky ground, where there wasn’t much soil. They quickly became dead because there was no depth in the ground.
verses.6: On the 1st of August, it began to grow again, but because it didn’t have roots, it withered away.
verses.7: But other things fell onto the flames. The flames then rose up and consumed those things.
verses.8: But other crops also fell onto the land, and they produced fruit. Some of these crops yielded ten units, others sixty, and still others thirty-three units.
verses.9: He who has that, listen carefully.
verses.10: And when the disciples came forward, they said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
verses.11: But the one who answered said to them: “Since you are given the knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, they are not given that knowledge.”
verses.12: For those who do have it, it will be given to them and increased in quantity. But those who don’t have it, what they already have will be taken away from them.
verses.13: Therefore, I speak to them in parables. For when they see, they do not see; when they hear, they do not hear either. They also do not make any sense of what they hear.
verses.14: And the prophecy of Esaias will be fulfilled for them. “Hearken, and do not forget; look, and do not despise.”
verses.15: For the hearts of this people have become hardened, and they cannot hear those who speak to them. Their eyes are also closed. But if they were to see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and if their hearts would listen as well, then I will be able to reach them.
verses.16: But it is better for your eyes to see, so that they can see; and it is better for your ears to hear, so that they can hear.
verses.17: Indeed, I tell you that many prophets and righteous people desired to see what you see, but they did not see; and to hear what you hear, but they did not hear.
verses.18: Thus, you have heard the parable of the sower.
verses.19: Everyone who listens to the words of the kingdom and does not follow them, will be led astray by the evil one, who steals away what is precious in their hearts. This is the person who is led astray along the wrong path.
verses.20: And he who spreads the word over the barren lands – that is, he who listens to the words and immediately accepts them with joy.
verses.21: It doesn’t have a root in itself; it’s rather a result of suffering or persecution due to that word.
verses.22: But those who are scattered among the wildflowers… these are those who listen to the word of God. The temptations of this world and the deceptions of wealth suppress the word of God, and thus they become like worthless seeds.
verses.23: And those who scatter themselves upon good land, these are those who listen to the words and act upon them. They cultivate the land, producing one crop here, fifty crops there, and thirty crops here too.
verses.24: Another parable was given to them, saying: The kingdom of heaven is like a man who went out to seed in his field.
verses.25: And when he tried to cross over the people, his enemy rushed forward and threw stones at him in the middle of the road. Then he left.
verses.26: And when the vineyard was planted and fruit was produced, then the fig trees also appeared.
verses.27: Then the slaves of the owner came and said to him, “Lord, did you not scatter good seed in the field? Then how can there be weeds?”
verses.28: And he said to them, “This man is a wicked person.” The slaves replied to him, “Do you really want us to collect those things when you leave?”
verses.29: He said: “Oh, maybe when you gathered the leaves, you should also give them a reward.”
verses.30: Please get together both of you until the time comes for the ceremony. And at the time of the ceremony, I will explain everything to those who are going to perform the ceremony. First, collect the spices and arrange them in bundles before applying them. Then, bring the sistrum into my storage place.
verses.31: Another parable was given to them, which said: “It is like a kingdom ruled by the light of heaven. A man took that light and scattered it in the field.”
verses.32: The smallest of all seeds is the one that grows into a tree when it grows larger than grains of wheat. Then, it becomes a tree, and its branches can be used as a place to sit and rest in the sky.
verses.33: He spoke another parable to them. It’s the same as the kingdom of heaven being hidden by a woman, who kept it hidden in a sachet until it was fully dried up.
verses.34: All these things said Jesus to the crowd in parables. But without any intention of being a parable, he also spoke to them directly.
verses.35: So that what has been prophesied by the prophet may be fulfilled: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will speak in secret from above.”
verses.36: Then, after getting rid of the crowd, he went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, “Please explain to us the parable of the fig trees.”
verses.37: And the one who answered said, “The one who sows good seed is the son of man.”
verses.38: And the field is the world itself. The “good seeds” are those who belong to the kingdom of God. The “bad seeds” are those who belong to the devil.
verses.39: And that evil spirit is actually Diablo himself. The “therisma” is a kind of summer, and those who practice thetherisma are actually angels.
verses.40: Just as the leaves are collected and burned, so too will it happen in the course of the summer.
verses.41: The son of man will appoint his messengers to carry out his commands. They will gather all the wickedness and those who commit injustice from his kingdom.
verses.42: And they will be thrown into the furnace of fire. There, they will suffer great pain and torment.
verses.43: Then, the righteous will shine like the sun in their father’s kingdom. He who has ears, may hear.
verses.44: It is the kingdom of the treasures in heaven, hidden in that field. A person who finds it hides it away. From his joy, he sells everything he has, and he buys that field from others.
verses.45: Once again, it is the same with the kingdom of heaven for those who are merchants and seek good magicians.
verses.46: After finding a very valuable merchant, he spent all that he had and bought him.
verses.47: Once again, the kingdom of heaven is thrown into the sea by the powerful forces of heaven; it is brought together from all directions.
verses.48: When they had completed their journey and sat down on the altar, they gathered together the good things for the offering, while the bad things were placed outside.
verses.49: So it will be in the conduct of this year. The messengers will be sent out, and they will cast out the evil ones from among the righteous.
verses.50: And they will be thrown into the furnace of fire. There, they will suffer great pain and torment.
verses.51: Did all these things happen? They say to him: “No.”
verses.52: And he said to them, “For this reason, every secretary who is trained in the kingdom of heaven is like a landlord who manages his own treasures. He can take out anything from those treasures, both new and old.”
verses.53: And it happened that when Jesus finished these parables, he left that place.
verses.54: And when he came back to his homeland, he taught them in their assembly. He made them understand that this wisdom and these abilities came from him.
verses.55: Isn’t this the son of the architect? Nor is it said that his mother’s name was Mariam. Nor are his brothers named Jacob, Joseph, Simon, and Judas.
verses.56: And aren’t his sisters also not willing to come to us? Where does this all come from then?
verses.57: And they were distressed in him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not worthy of trust unless he is recognized in his own country and among his own family.”
verses.58: And he did not use many forces there, due to their lack of trust in him.
